title: Service Desk Queue
description: Bucket board for open requests (tickets) in one Jira Service Management service desk -- redesigned from the earlier flat-list version (same tile, same WorkQ ticket: 'Tile: Service Desk Queue - JSM - Service Management') to a Dataverse-tile-inspired click-to-filter layout. A header badge shows the count of requests whose 'Time to resolution' SLA clock has already breached, next to an opt-in 'Check SLA % this month' button (first-response compliance over tickets resolved this calendar month) implemented via `atlassian_check_sla_this_month`, this plugin's first widget-element ACTION (not just a function/component) -- see that action's own JSDoc in `widget-elements/src/index.ts` for the full mechanics, including why it deliberately diverges from myHubV2's `expand_github_item` reference pattern on exactly one point (a plain same-origin `fetch()` of `/api/widgets-system/call-tool` instead of an unreachable host-bundle import). Deliberately on-demand only, never automatic: computing it needs a JQL search for tickets resolved this month plus one `get_request_sla` lookup PER resolved ticket (N+1), capped at 100 tickets (most-recent-resolved-first) to bound the cost of one click -- if more than 100 resolved tickets exist this month, the result says so plainly ("-- more exist") rather than presenting a capped number as complete, since Jira's current search endpoint doesn't return a total match count to compare against. A ticket resolved this month whose "Time to first response" SLA has no completed cycle at all (no SLA policy on that request type) is excluded from both the numerator and denominator, not guessed at. The button's `project_key` param ("SUP", this sandbox's JQL project key -- distinct from the numeric `service_desk_id` used elsewhere on this tile) is hardcoded for the same reason `service_desk_id` is below: no dataProvider-chaining support exists yet to resolve it live from `list_service_desks`. Below the header, four large stat cards -- New / In Progress / Behind / Alerts -- are computed client-side from the SAME single `list_service_desk_requests` call already fetched by this tile's `dataProvider` (no second tool call): New = `currentStatus.statusCategory === "NEW"` (Jira's own UPPERCASE category key, confirmed against Atlassian's servicedeskapi docs and a real live sandbox sample that showed `"INDETERMINATE"` for a 'Waiting for support' ticket -- do not confuse this flat string with the platform Issue API's nested, lowercase `fields.status.statusCategory.key`, a different shape entirely); Alerts = the 'Time to resolution' SLA's `ongoingCycle.breached === true` (same definition as the header's breached counter -- their counts are EXPECTED to match exactly, not a bug); Behind = that same clock not yet breached but at-risk, reusing the exact 15%-of-goal-duration / 1h-fallback threshold already implemented in `atlassian_sla_tone`'s warning logic; In Progress = everything else not caught by Alerts/Behind/New (typically `statusCategory === "INDETERMINATE"`). Bucket priority is SLA-urgency-first (Alerts > Behind > New > In Progress) so an unactioned brand-new ticket already close to breaching doesn't hide under New -- see `atlassian_request_bucket` in this plugin's widget-elements for the full reasoning. Clicking a card selects that bucket (a plain widget-local `/ui/selectedBucket` state path -- clicking the already-selected card deselects it back to the no-selection prompt state, the same toggle-on-reclick pattern already proven in this marketplace's HubSpot/Salesforce support-ticket tiles) and reveals a request list filtered to it below, capped at 20 rows per TILE-DISPLAY-STANDARDS.md §11 (the same `dataProvider` limit as before -- filtering only ever narrows that set, never re-fetches). **Platform gotcha found and worked around while building this tile:** the filtered list is NOT a per-row `visible` check comparing a `$computed` bucket against `/ui/selectedBucket` -- confirmed live in the tile harness that this renderer's `visible`/`$cond` condition grammar only recognizes `$state`/`$item`/`$index` as the primary operand key (RULE 5.9 in `myHubV2/architecture/technical/mobile-widget-interpreter.md`); a condition keyed on `$computed` silently evaluates as absent/falsy every time, with or without a comparator, hiding every row (or always taking a `$cond`'s `$else` branch) regardless of the actual computed value. Worked around by pre-filtering: `card.watch` recomputes `/ui/filteredRequests` (via `atlassian_filter_by_bucket`) whenever the source data or `/ui/selectedBucket` changes, and `requestList.repeat.statePath` points at that already-filtered array instead of filtering per row. The header's breached-count badge tone has the same shape fix: `atlassian_bucket_tone` returns the tone string directly rather than a `$cond` branching on a `$computed` condition. No bucket is selected on load; the space below the cards shows a plain prompt until one is clicked. Each row keeps this tile's exact pre-existing click-through behavior unchanged: opens the real ticket in Jira via the request's own `_links.agent` URL (wrapped through the `identity` computed helper, since a bare `$item` inside an action param resolves to a state PATH, not its value) in a new tab. Agent-facing only -- shows every request visible to the connected admin/agent account, not a per-customer 'my tickets' view (that remains a deliberate, deferred follow-up needing a personal-connection rollout model this plugin's other tiles don't use). **Known platform limitation carried over unchanged from the prior version: `service_desk_id` is genuinely site-specific and this widget cannot auto-resolve it** -- a widget's `dataProvider` fires exactly one MCP tool call on mount, so it can't call `list_service_desks` first and feed the result into this call. The `service_desk_id` shipped below is the connected sandbox's own 'Support' desk, used only to prove this tile end-to-end against real data -- call `list_service_desks` and edit `dataProvider.params.service_desk_id` before enabling it for any other tenant. **Confirmed real limitation on the New bucket:** the default JSM 'IT support' template's workflow (verified directly against a live site's workflow diagram) has no To-Do-category status at all -- its START node flows straight into a status Jira itself categorizes as INDETERMINATE ('Waiting for support'), so a ticket is never truly 'NEW' by Jira's own data model on this template. The bucket logic itself is correct and general (`statusCategory === "NEW"` is exactly how Jira represents a To-Do-category status anywhere), but expect New to read 0 on any service desk using this common default template -- it will only populate for a customer whose workflow has been customized to include a real To-Do-category status. This is a per-customer workflow-configuration limitation, not a bug in this tile.
